senses.sense_definition: Relating to or characteristic of an earlier period; old-fashioned or antiquated.

examples.text: The building has an <w>archaic</w> design that reminds visitors of the nineteenth century.
Many people consider the current tax system to be <w>archaic</w> and in need of reform.

senses.sense_definition: No longer in common use, but occasionally employed to evoke a sense of the past.

examples.text: The poet used <w>archaic</w> language to give the verses a sense of historical depth.
Some readers find it difficult to understand the <w>archaic</w> terms found in Shakespearean plays.

traits.comment: Refers to language or customs that are no longer current.

senses.sense_definition: Relating to the earliest stages of a historical or cultural period.

examples.text: The museum exhibit focuses on <w>archaic</w> pottery styles from the early Greek period.
Archaeologists discovered several <w>archaic</w> tools at the excavation site near the river.

senses.sense_definition: An early or ancestral variety of human, such as a Neanderthal.

examples.text: Scientists continue to study the remains of various <w>archaics</w> to understand human evolution.
The study compares modern humans with earlier <w>archaics</w> found in the same region.

senses.sense_definition: A specific prehistoric period in the Americas between the earliest human presence and later agricultural societies.

examples.text: The <w>Archaic</w> was a time when hunter-gatherer groups adapted to diverse environments.
Evidence of the <w>Archaic</w> can be seen in the stone tools found across the continent.
